title: Adaptive viewport strategies for dense tables and GPU-accelerated charts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a coordinated set of responsive rules and engineering patterns to ensure Redwood Console pages (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) render consistently and performantly across modern and legacy browsers. This ticket covers: dense data tables with virtualization and sticky headers, GPU-accelerated canvas/SVG chart rendering at high DPR, modal stacking and focus management, and targeted fallbacks for Safari (iOS/macOS), Firefox, and legacy Edge.

Goals:
- Ensure tables remain readable and navigable at narrow widths without breaking layouts or hiding important columns.
- Maintain sub-100ms perceived scroll latency with virtualized rows and sticky column headers on mid-range devices.
- Guarantee charts render crisply at high DPR and don't become pixelated or janky during resize/zoom.
- Fix modal stacking, z-index, and focus-trap regressions observed in multi-modal flows (e.g., open rollout modal on top of cost breakdown); ensure keyboard and screen-reader access.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
1) Table responsive strategy: column prioritization + column collapse into detail drawer vs. horizontal scroll. We prototyped both. The chosen pattern is: show a minimal column set at narrow widths and provide a persistent "peek" affordance that opens a row-detail drawer. This keeps important metrics visible and avoids horizontal scrolling on mobile. Trade-off: extra interaction to view hidden data; mitigated with clear affordances and remembered user preference.

2) Virtualization + sticky header: combine row virtualization (windowing) with CSS sticky header. On Safari we observed sticky headers changing stacking contexts when using transform on parent containers. Workaround: avoid transform on the scrolling container, use will-change: transform only where necessary, and position sticky at top-level scroll container. Engineering will add a small wrapper to ensure correct context.

3) Charts: Use GPU-accelerated canvas rendering for large time-series, with SVG fallback for small sparkline widgets. For Safari < 16 and older Firefox, offscreen canvas isn't available; we add an explicit single-threaded canvas fallback and do progressive paint (draw low-res first, then refine). Also use window.devicePixelRatio-aware scaling to keep strokes crisp.

4) Modal stacking and focus: implement a modal manager that enforces a strict stacking order, adds aria-hidden to background content, and ensures focus trap across nested modals. Accessibility audit flagged missing tabindex management for rollouts modal when a nested settings modal opens — fixed in prototype by re-focusing last active element and persisting keyboard navigation order.

Current progress:
- 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with PM/Eng. Agreed on column-prioritization rules and chart fallbacks.
- 2026-02-24: First mobile + narrow-breakpoint prototype completed (TableView-Mobile). Validated priority columns with PM and two customer support reps.
- 2026-03-02: Design review with ENG team. ENG proposed using IntersectionObserver for virtualization triggers and an engineering wrapper to avoid transform stacking context issues.
- 2026-03-05: Eng PR #8321 opened (basic virtualization + sticky header wrapper).
- 2026-03-08: Usability sync: testers reported a discoverability gap for the row-detail drawer on small screens; we added a persistent chevron affordance and microcopy.
- 2026-03-10: QA found z-index regression in Edge (sticky header hidden behind native scrollbar on Windows 11). Root cause: overflow:auto + scrollbar-gutter interaction. Engineering to add scrollbar-gutter: stable and adjust header z-index and painting order.
- 2026-03-11: Accessibility pass: aria-live region added for dynamic row details; keyboard order verified in VoiceOver and NVDA for primary flows.

Next steps:
- ENG to land PR #8321 with updated wrapper and scrollbar-gutter fix.
- Design to finalize microcopy and small-screen affordance animations (reduce motion fallback).
- QA to run cross-browser regression matrix across macOS Safari (iOS simulation), iOS Safari 16/17, Firefox latest, Edge (Chromium), and legacy Edge where available.
- Plan a staged rollout: feature-flagged canary for 5% of traffic, monitor console-2026.03 telemetry for scroll latency and error rates.

2026-02-25 Sofia Martinez: Uploaded mobile-first prototype to Figma. Noted pitfalls with horizontal scroll on small devices; recommend drawer pattern as fallback.
2026-03-02 Anika Patel (Eng): Reviewed prototype - suggested IntersectionObserver for virtualization and to avoid transforms on scroll container. I'll prototype a wrapper component.
2026-03-08 QA - Rahul Singh: Found discoverability issue for collapsed columns on small screens. Added suggestion to include persistent affordance + onboarding tooltip.
2026-03-10 Evan Brooks (Eng): PR #8321 opened with virtualization + sticky header wrapper. Found Edge scrollbar-gutter issues; will add patch in follow-up PR.

acceptance_criteria: Tables: at <= 480px the primary metric columns remain visible; hidden columns accessible via a row-detail drawer
Virtualization + sticky headers: scrolling stable across macOS Safari, Firefox, Edge with no header flicker
Charts: high-DPR devices render without pixelation; Safari/Firefox fallback must show progressive paint with final fidelity
Modals: nested modal flows maintain focus trap and background content is aria-hidden; keyboard navigation preserved
Cross-browser QA: no regressions in scroll latency (95th percentile < 120ms perceived) on our medium-device lab
